report: A quiet day for our book. No orders were sent and nothing filled, so there were no trading costs today. The trader held its one position: 6 Infineon shares bought at 50.90 euros on 10 November. Infineon closed at 49.21, up from 48.69, a day gain of 3.12 euros, or 0.16 percent. The position is still about 10 euros under water. The stop is about 46.82, roughly 2.40 euros or 5 percent below today's price. The exit date is 24 November, four trading days away. The reason to hold is unchanged: a record quarter and guidance of over 20 percent growth, and analyst target cuts do not walk that guidance back. The background is still risk-off: VIX above 25, gold near a one and a half year low, copper at its lowest since July, and Brent below our 98 dollar bar. Equity is 1,987.35 euros, cash 1,692.12, total minus 0.63 percent. Reconcile is consistent and there were no warnings. Two odd things: this input has no new market news, and an earlier reviewer run already wrote a handoff for this same day. Today's small gain is noise. One open position cannot show skill. No trade has closed and no shadow call has scored yet.
questions: The Infineon stop sits about 5 percent below the price with four trading days left. Should a stop that will probably never be reached before the exit date change, or is the time exit doing the real work?

Two reviewer runs were made for 2026-11-18, and an earlier input had quotes about 878 minutes old at decision time. Should the pipeline stop a second run on the same day and refuse to decide on quotes that old?

The rule says buy only when the expected move is well above twice the entry cost, yet nothing has qualified for eight days. Is that bar right for a 2,000 euro account, or does it mean we mostly hold cash?
